note: Proposed NEW JFR events derived from gap analysis of -Xlog log sites that no existing JFR event covers. These events DO NOT exist in the JDK 26 oracle (196 events); they are candidates for upstream proposal. Scope of this analysis: -Xlog:trimnative*,gc*,gc+region*,gc+ergo*,gc+humongous*,stringdedup*=info (127 uncovered firing sites). Each 'replaces' entry cites the HotSpot source file + verbatim log format string the event would make recoverable via JFR. Field types follow the oracle convention (long for time/bytes/counters, int for ids, float/double for ratios, boolean/String). startTime/duration follow the standard JFR event contract. Status note (2026-08-17): JDK 26 (196 events) added jdk.StringDeduplication + jdk.FinalFieldMutation vs JDK 25 (194 events). JDK 27-dev master adds jdk.ShenandoahPromotionInformation. JDK-8365306 (NativeHeapTrim JFR, PR #26756, closed 2025-12): PR was blocked on ProcessSize umbrella design — narrow trim-only re-proposal recommended. G1 now has UseGCOverheadLimit (JDK-8212084, merged JDK 26, PR #27950) but no JFR event. JEP 521 Generational Shenandoah became production-ready in JDK 25. None of the other proposed events have upstream work in progress as of 2026-08-17. Critique pass 4 applied 2026-08-17: confirmed 0 of 18 proposals are covered by JDK 26/27-dev; promoted G1CollectionSetCandidates (corrected from working doc — two separate candidate paths: marking + retained) and G1HeapResize (drivers from g1HeapSizingPolicy.cpp) to JSON; added note on ShenandoahCollectionDecision zScore/marginOfError (belong to post-cycle path, NOT the decision point); ZForwardingRemembered kept as lower-priority note (log lines print addresses not counts, no aggregation infrastructure exists); G1PeriodicGCCheck / G1ConcurrentMarkTaskStats / GCWorkerConfiguration / G1RegionLivenessUpdate kept as notes in NEW_EVENTS.md.

proposed.label: String Deduplication Statistics
proposed.status: REDUNDANT — jdk.StringDeduplication shipped in JDK 26 (PR #28015) with fields: inspected, known, shared, newStrings, newSize(bytes), replaced, deleted, deduplicated, deduplicatedSize(bytes), skippedDead, skippedIncomplete, skippedShared, processing(Tickspan), tableResize(Tickspan), tableCleanup(Tickspan). The only genuinely new fields this event would add over JDK 26 are cumulative totals: totalDedupedBytes and totalNewUnknownBytes (per-cycle values are already covered). If pursuing upstream, propose adding these two fields plus dedupedRatio to the existing jdk.StringDeduplication event rather than creating a new event.
proposed.rationale: JDK 26 added jdk.StringDeduplication (JDK-8037914/PR #28015) covering per-cycle byte-level data including newSize, deduplicatedSize, and timing. The remaining gap is cumulative totals only. Note: gcId must NOT be added — string deduplication runs concurrently on a dedicated thread and is not tied to any single GC cycle.

proposed.label: Shenandoah Card Statistics
proposed.rationale: Shenandoah generational (only, JEP 521 production-ready in JDK 25) remembered-set card scanning emits cumulative dirty/clean card statistics per GC cycle with no JFR event. IMPORTANT: the log() method is wrapped in #ifndef PRODUCT — this event would only fire in debug/fastdebug builds unless the JFR emission point is moved to a product-build path. The per-worker stats are gated behind ShenandoahEnableCardStats (non-product); this event emits only the cumulative aggregate. dirtyScannedObjects maps to _dirty_scan_obj_cnt — the count of heap objects visited as a result of dirty card scans (distinct from dirtyCards = card-table slot count). maxConsecutiveDirtyCards reflects card-table clustering that affects scan efficiency.

proposed.label: Shenandoah Minimum Mutator Utilization
proposed.rationale: Shenandoah's MMU tracker prints GC utilization (GCU) and mutator utilization (MU) per completed phase with no JFR analogue. NOT redundant with jdk.G1MMU: G1MMU measures pause-time compliance within a fixed time-slice window (gcTime vs pauseTarget in ms); ShenandoahMMU measures GCU%/MU% utilization fractions over the entire phase window — semantically different metrics answering different questions. Low muPercent directly indicates mutator starvation. There are TWO distinct emission paths: (1) update_utilization() at end of each GC cycle; (2) report() periodic-sample path (every ~5s). isPeriodicSample boolean distinguishes them. gcId from _most_recent_gcid is needed for GC event correlation.

proposed.label: Shenandoah Reclaim Progress
proposed.rationale: shenandoahMetrics.cpp's is_good_progress() evaluates four independent dimensions after each cycle. IMPORTANT early-exit semantics: the function returns on the FIRST dimension that passes (or after free-space fails) — not all 4 dimensions are logged every cycle. Fields for dimensions 2-4 are NULLABLE. Fragmentation values are fractions (0.0-1.0) in source; stored as percentage (0.0-100.0) here for usability. freeNeeded = (softMaxCapacity/100) * ShenandoahCriticalFreeThreshold (bytes). usedNeededToFree = ShenandoahHeapRegion::region_size_bytes() — effectively a fixed constant. goodProgress=false in any dimension signals risk of degenerated GC fallback. Note: _consecutive_degenerated_gcs_without_progress from ShenandoahCollectorPolicy is a high-value additional field — if it reaches CONSECUTIVE_BAD_DEGEN_PROGRESS_THRESHOLD (2) a Full GC fires next.

proposed.label: ZGC NMethod Registration
proposed.rationale: ZGC requires all nmethods to have load barriers patched (registered). Field semantics from ZNMethodTable.cpp: registeredNMethods = _nregistered (current live count); staleNMethodSlots = _nunregistered (entries unregistered but not yet pruned — zombie entries pending table rebuild, NOT a cumulative total). tableRebuilt: DESIGN GAP — no per-cycle tableRebuilt boolean exists in ZStatNMethods::print(); requires new instrumentation. Production validation: low — no external evidence found that nmethod table overhead is a common production problem. Recommend de-prioritizing.

proposed.label: GC Overhead Limit Exceeded
proposed.rationale: Fires immediately before the JVM throws OutOfMemoryError: GC Overhead Limit exceeded. Now implemented in both G1 (JDK-8212084, merged JDK 26 PR #27950) and Parallel GC — but no JFR event was added. Parallel GC logs TWO separate free-space values (young + old gen); G1 logs one combined value. gcTimePercent: G1 uses long_term_gc_time_ratio()*100; Parallel uses 100-mutator_time_percent(). consecutiveViolations = _gc_overhead_counter (resets to zero on a clean GC; fires OOM at GCOverheadLimitThreshold=5). gcId is GCId::peek() — last completed GC id (approximate).

proposed.label: Native Heap Trim
proposed.rationale: The JVM periodically calls malloc_trim/madvise to return RSS to the OS (NativeHeapTrimmer thread, -XX:TrimNativeHeapInterval). Especially valuable on containerised deployments. JDK-8365306 (PR #26756) was closed 2025-12 — the NativeHeapTrim event itself was not objected to; a narrow trim-only re-proposal is recommended. deltaBytes is SIGNED: afterBytes - beforeBytes (negative = RSS reduced, positive = RSS grew). trimCount = _num_trims_performed (uint64_t, first = 1). detailsAvailable=false when /proc/self/status unavailable.

proposed.label: G1 Concurrent Refinement Sweep
proposed.rationale: G1 concurrent refinement sweeps the dirty-card queue (DCQS) between pauses. Fires once per sweep (potentially multiple times per GC pause). Log format verified from source: print_refinement_stats() starts with 'Refinement took %.2fms'. The JDK 25 write barrier redesign (JEP 522) changed refinement behavior significantly — this event is needed to understand the new refinement dynamics. cardsNoCrossRegion (no_cross_region in source) = within-region references filtered early; high = good heap locality. All fields verified against actual g1ConcurrentRefine.cpp format string.

proposed.label: G1 Collection Set Candidates
proposed.rationale: G1's mixed-GC region selection reasoning is entirely invisible in JFR today. jdk.EvacuationInformation records the outcome (regions evacuated, bytes); this event records the DECISION: how many candidates were available, how many selected, whether time budget was exceeded, and why mixed GCs stopped. There are TWO separate candidate paths: (1) MARKING candidates — regions identified by concurrent marking as high-garbage; (2) RETAINED candidates — regions from previous cycles that were deferred. Both paths have equivalent log structures and should be covered by a single event with a candidateType discriminator. IMPORTANT corrections from source audit: (1) proposed 'predictedTimeExceeded' boolean does not exist as a variable — source has 'Added %u ... although the predicted time was too high' (count of over-budget regions added). (2) 'reason' enum is implementable but requires synthesizing from three distinct stop conditions. (3) 'groups' (card-set groups, not region count) is logged separately and adds context. (4) predicted initial/optional times and optional threshold are available from the Finish log. No existing event covers this; jdk.G1AdaptiveIHOP/jdk.G1BasicIHOP cover IHOP (marking trigger), not collection-set selection.

proposed.label: G1 Heap Resize Decision
proposed.rationale: G1's adaptive heap resize (expand/shrink) is driven by CPU-usage feedback in g1HeapSizingPolicy.cpp. The size delta is computable from jdk.G1HeapSummary before/after, but the DRIVERS (short/long-term GC-CPU-usage %, thresholds, scale factor, which trigger fired) are in no existing event — these are the actual tuning signal for G1ExpandByPercent / GCTimeRatio. Not covered by jdk.G1AdaptiveIHOP (which covers old-gen occupancy threshold for marking, not heap capacity resize). Field corrections from source audit: (1) 'reason' DOES NOT EXIST as a source variable — the decision is driven by _gc_cpu_usage_deviation_counter reaching G1CPUUsageExpandThreshold or -G1CPUUsageShrinkThreshold. (2) freeRegions and regionsNeededForAlloc come from SHRINK LOG ONLY — null/0 for expansion. (3) scaleFactor is shrink-path-only. (4) 'Heap resize triggers' log is at TRACE level (not debug). (5) The expand log has lowerThreshold/upperThreshold/gcCpuUsageTarget — missing from original proposal. direction = expand (bool in source, tristate derivable from expand + resize_bytes==0).

proposed.label: ZGC Director Rule Evaluation
proposed.rationale: ZGC's director evaluates rules to decide whether to trigger GC. IMPORTANT design notes: (1) Early-exit: make_minor/major_gc_decision return on first triggered rule — at most one Minor and one Major rule fires per cycle. (2) rule_minor_allocation_rate_static (UseDynamicNumberOfGCThreads=false) is a separate variant with NO gcCPUTime/gcWorkers/allocRateVariancePct. (3) Proactive rule has TWO mutually exclusive branches (enabled vs not-yet-enabled). (4) rule_major_allocation_rate is an ESCALATION rule from start_gc(), not make_major_gc_decision(). (5) Timer rule applies to both generations. (6) High Usage log has freePercent. Generation values 'Young'/'Old' align with JFR convention.

proposed.label: Parallel GC Adaptive Size Policy
proposed.rationale: Parallel GC's AdaptiveSizePolicy runs a feedback loop after each GC to resize eden and survivor. Field corrections: (1) minMutatorIntervalSec REMOVED — does not exist. (2) throughputEdenIncrease is branch-specific (throughput-increase path only, always positive). (3) pauseMs renamed to minorPauseMs (major GC not included). (4) mutatorIntervalSec/Last renamed to gcDistanceSec/Last (source: _gc_distance_seconds_seq). (5) throughputGoal: no stored field; re-derived from GCTimeRatio flag. (6) desiredEden/Survivor: must be captured at PSYoungGen call site. (7) promotedBytesEstimate/Last are floating-point doubles.

proposed.label: Shenandoah Collection Decision
proposed.rationale: Shenandoah generational mode's regulator/control FSM decides each cycle what to collect. Field corrections: (1) immediateGarbagePercent REMOVED — source uses immediate_garbage (bytes) + immediate_regions (count). (2) decision: synthesized from GCMode enum (none/concurrent_normal/stw_degenerated/stw_full/servicing_old/bootstrapping_old/stopped) + regulator path. (3) This event spans MULTIPLE code sites — no single function emits all fields. NOTE on zScore/marginOfError: shenandoahAdaptiveHeuristics.cpp has 'z-score=%.3f' and 'Margin of error now %.2f' logs (both log_debug(gc, ergo)), but these fire in record_success_concurrent() AFTER a GC completes — NOT at the should_start_gc() decision point. They belong to a separate post-cycle accounting path and should NOT be added to this decision event. marginOfError could be included as a 'current confidence interval width' since it directly affects the next decision.
